references.text: Also mentions Ataroth-addar as a boundary city, confirming the border line between the territories of Ephraim and Benjamin.
Describes the lower boundary of Joseph's sons going down to Beth-horon, complementing the description of Ephraim's border.
Beth-horon is mentioned as the place where the Lord cast large stones from heaven upon the enemies, highlighting the city's strategic importance.
States that Serah, daughter of Ephraim, built Lower and Upper Beth-horon, linking the city to the tribe of Ephraim.
Lists the descendants of Ephraim and their clans, providing background for the tribal inheritance mentioned in this verse.
Jacob adopts Ephraim and Manasseh as his own sons, explaining why Ephraim received his own tribal portion.
